item.title: Kyle Shanahan Rules Brock Purdy Out For Seahawks Clash
item.description: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images An ankle injury will cause San Francisco 49ers quarterback Brock Purdy to miss Sunday’s game against the Seattle Seahawks, according to head coach Kyle Shanahan on Friday. Mac Jones takes over as the starter, with Kurtis Rourke serving as the backup, according to ESPN reporter Nick Wagoner. The team made this call after Purdy did not practice all week and his injury did not heal fast enough to allow him to suit up. During the second quarter of last week’s victory over the Minnesota Vikings, Purdy injured his left ankle. The injury happened when Purdy tried to escape defensive lineman Jalen Redmond and his foot bent awkwardly as he went to the ground. Shanahan knew about the issue at halftime but said it did not change how he called plays for the rest of that game. The coach ruled the injury out on Friday because it simply did not improve during the week. A Mid-Level Ankle Issue Shanahan explained the specific nature of the injury while speaking to reporters on Friday. “Anytime it’s not a high ankle sprain, you get pretty relieved, but it was more mid than low, which is a little bit worse,” Shanahan said. He noted that the team had a feeling by Wednesday that Purdy would not be ready. “Kind of had a feeling just the way it was by the time Wednesday came around. [It] didn’t heal up as fast as we wanted, so had to shut him down,” the coach added. Purdy does not require surgery, and the expectation is that he will be ready for Week 13 versus the New York Giants. Shanahan remains optimistic about the timeline for his recovery. “It’s too soon [to tell] but I’m pretty optimistic about it,” Shanahan said. He acknowledged the sudden change in plans but expressed hope for the future. “But I was about this week to start and then it changes. So, hopefully it’ll be all right,” he told the press. Mac Jones Steps Up Again Jones is no stranger to this situation for the 49ers. In 2025, when Purdy suffered a turf toe injury, he started eight games in Purdy’s stead. During those contests, the 49ers went 5-3 with Jones posting a 62.7 QBR. He threw for 2,151 yards, 13 touchdowns, and six interceptions in that span. This season, Jones has seen action only in mop-up duty, where he completed one pass on one attempt for 5 yards. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Left tackle Trent Williams voiced strong support for Jones after seeing his preparation this week. Williams highlighted the team’s confidence in him based on his past performance. “He was great last year when we needed him,” Williams said. The team expects Jones to handle the pressure of this big divisional game. “We expect him to be good this year,” Williams added. Shanahan praised Jones for his work during the week leading up to the matchup. “Mac’s been awesome,” Shanahan said. “He’s had a great week. We went through this with him last year, so everyone’s got a ton of confidence in Mac. Mac’s had a hell of a camp, and he’s the same guy every day. It’s been a good week with Mac,” per ProFoo

item.title: Iowa’s Hank Brown Proves CFP Dreams Are Real Again
item.description: Iowa Hawkeyes running back L.J. Phillips Jr. (21) carries the ball against Nebraska Cornhuskers linebacker Vincent Shavers Jr. (10) and Nebraska Cornhuskers defensive back Caleb Benning (28) Nov. 27, 2026 during a Big Ten football game at Kinnick Stadium in Iowa City, Iowa. The No. 13 Hawkeyes crushed Nebraska 31-7 , marking their fifth straight victory. Brown scored three rushing touchdowns and added one passing touchdown. Iowa returns to contention for a Big Ten Championship Game berth and gains national attention thanks to this showing. The team now sits at 10-2 overall with a 7-2 record in the Big Ten conference. A loss would have ended their season, but this win keeps the door open for a national title run. While Brown shined with the ball, the Iowa defense shut the door on Nebraska completely. The unit allowed only five total touchdowns during this five-game winning streak. They held the Huskers scoreless in the second half for the third straight game in a row. Iowa leads the entire nation in scoring defense right now. The offense outgained Nebraska 329 yards to 260 yards, which was the first time a team has done so against Nebraska this season. Nebraska tried to fight back after winning against Ohio State the week before, but they could not stop the Hawkeyes. The Huskers recovered a muffed punt in the third quarter while trailing 10-7, yet they failed to score on that drive. After a third-down stop at the Iowa 35-yard line, they surrendered a score on the following drive. Jamal Rule rushed for 106 yards and scored a 21-yard touchdown for Nebraska in the second quarter. Despite his efforts, the Huskers fell to 7-5 overall and 4-5 in conference play. There are still specific combinations that must occur for Iowa to reach the Big Ten Championship Game. However, their path to the national playoffs remains clear if they keep winning. The Associated Press reported that the Hawkeyes have outscored their opponents 147-41 during this current winning streak. Brown opened the scoring with a 14-yard run in the first quarter. With 4:02 remaining, his 29-yard run ended the scoring. Against the Huskers, Iowa has claimed 11 victories in their last 12 matchups.

item.title: BEFORE THE ROAR: LSU looks to finish regular season with a win at Arkansas
item.description: BATON ROUGE, LOUISIANA - SEPTEMBER 26: Quarterback Landen Clark #11 of the LSU Tigers celebrates after a touchdown during the second half of a game at Tiger Stadium on September 26, 2026 in Baton Rouge, Louisiana. (Photo by Tyler Kaufman/Getty Images) | Getty Images Game Notes: Time and Date: Saturday, November 28 at 11:45 a.m. CT Network: SEC Network Radio: LSU Sports Radio Network (Chris Blair, Jacob Hester, Gordy Rush) Location: Donald W. Reynolds Razorback Stadium, Fayetteville, Arkansas Spread: LSU -14.5 O/U 49.5 ESPN FPI: LSU 88% chance of winning End the Skid The Bayou Bengals certainly need something to feel positive about after losing the last three contests. They are a heavy road favorite in this one and should take care of business, giving them some sense of momentum heading into their bowl game and into 2027. Don’t Force the Ball LSU’s offense has done a really poor job of forcing the football into situations or areas where it didn’t need to in order to make a play, which has led to some really unfortunate turnovers or missed chances at points. If I’m the LSU offense, I am taking what Arkansas gives me and move the ball down the field methodically. There’s no need for hero ball in the season finale of a five-loss season. Block Out the Noise (again) The Tigers will once again have to block out the fact that they are the talk of the college football world as the SEC looks to remove them from the conference for the second time in 3 months. There will likely be jeers and comments from the opposing team or fans, but you have to block that out and stay disciplined. Do your job and let the performance on the field in what *could be * your final game in the SEC speak for itself.

item.title: Rams steal journeyman TE off 49ers’ practice squad
item.description: Gary A. Vasquez-Imagn Images Rams steal journeyman TE off 49ers’ practice squad appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . With the Los Angeles Rams getting bit by the injury bug, they turned to a division rival for a much-needed reinforcement. On Friday, the Rams announced that Tyler Higbee and Davis Allen are week-to-week due to a chest concussion and a high-ankle sprain, respectively, leaving the roster thin at tight end. With Higbee and Allen sidelined, Los Angeles added Jack Stoll, as reported by NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “The Rams are signing TE Jack Stoll off the (San Francisco) 49ers’ practice squad. With Tyler Higbee (chest) and Davis Allen (ankle) injured, Sean McVay & Co. bring in the veteran Stoll as part of the mix,” wrote Garafolo on X. The Rams acquired an experienced option to try to stem the tide while Higbee and Allen are out. Stoll is not exactly a household name, but he could be a good fit for McVay’s three-tight-end approach. Last season, Stoll played 15 games for the New Orleans Saints, tallying six receptions for 46 yards and one touchdown. Stoll, who was undrafted in 2021, has also spent time with the Philadelphia Eagles (two stints), the New York Giants, the Miami Dolphins, and the Cleveland Browns. He won a ring with the Eagles in 2025. His most productive campaign was in Philadelphia in 2022. In 17 games, including 11 starts, he had 11 receptions for 123 yards. Stoll could suit up in Week 13 against the Kansas City Chiefs at SoFi Stadium. The Rams will look for their sixth straight win, while the Chiefs will try to bounce back after falling to the Buffalo Bills on Thanksgiving Day. item.title: 49ers-Seahawks roundtable: How much will who's under center matter?
item.description: Sam Darnold #14 of the Seattle Seahawks passes the ball while being pressured by Romello Height #94 of the San Francisco 49ers during the first quarter at Lumen Field on Oct. 11, 2026 in Seattle. (Steph Chambers/Getty Images) When the San Francisco 49ers traveled to Seattle to play the Seahawks seven weeks ago, it represented a big moment for both teams. The 49ers won, remaining undefeated, and have gone 4-1 since. After narrowly losing, the Seahawks have stumbled to 3-2. With Kyle Shanahan 's club riding high and leading the NFC but facing a game with Brock Purdy on the sidelines, we asked columnist Ann Killion and reporters Eric Branch and Harrison Rich for their answers to these key questions going into Sunday's rematch. First, a general NFL question: the drama in Pittsburgh. Have we seen the last of Aaron Rodgers in uniform? Harrison Rich: It's often hard to side with Aaron Rodgers, but he seems to have the stronger argument here over Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy. ESPN confirmed Rodgers' allegations against McCarthy , including sleeping in quarterback meetings and breaking down a halftime huddle by saying "1-2-3 Packers." Rodgers was waived Wednesday, but I'd imagine he plays football again in 2026 - assuming he wants to. He was still playing at a fairly high level and led Pittsburgh to a 6-4 record before his ousting. Eric Branch: The constant in Aaron Rodgers' family and work drama: Aaron Rodgers. Given the late-career strife he's often been responsible for causing, it's notable that Rodgers' 22-season career began with him spending three good-soldier seasons sitting behind Brett Favre. Rodgers took a flamethrower to his long relationship with Mike McCarthy. It sounds as if much of what he alleged is true, but he broke an NFL code and left his playoff-contending teammates to deal with the fallout. Has he played his last snap? Not if an injury to a starting QB creates an urgent need. As former Cardinals GM Steve Keim once said of NFL teams rationalizing character concerns: "If Hannibal Lecter ran a 4.3, we'd probably diagnose it as an eating disorder." Ann Killion: I wouldn't be shocked if some playoff-bound team suffers an injury at quarterback and brings Rodgers in. I mean, who would be better? But, as the Black Friday broadcast team pointed out, Rodgers had already said this is his last year and has also emphasized that when he was done playing he will pull a "Keyser Soze" and disappear from public view. (Interesting to hear fellow former Cal Bear Tony Gonzalez put Rodgers on blast.) Yet there he was, airing his dirty laundry on the Pat McAfee show, blowtorching the coach he won a Super Bowl with, and texting Al Michaels during the Friday broadcast to further litigate his case. The guy desperately needs the spotlight. Pittsburgh crushed Denver, sending the message that they don't need Rodgers (though the players all still seem to like him). Rodgers' most amazing feat? Turning hapless McCarthy into a sympathetic character. Fred Warner

item.title: Nebraska Football Fails To Deliver With The Bright Lights Placed On The Program
item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Matt Rhule and Nebraska had an underwhelming performance in 31-7 loss to Iowa on Black Friday. Nebraska football has done enough to warrant Matt Rhule having another crack at things. But Black Friday was not one to remember for Husker Nation. Related: Iowa Earns Its Spot Inside The College Football Playoff Field Coming off quite possibly the biggest win in the coaching career of Rhule at Nebraska, the Huskers laid a massive egg. Iowa scored a 31-7 victory, continuing its domination in the series. Instead of riding the momentum generated by the win over Ohio State, the Huskers looked like the Nebraska of old. Uninspired. Iowa’s Offense Completely Dominated Nebraska It all started on the defensive side of the football for the Huskers. The Hawkeyes had over 300 yards of total offense, as Hank Brown ran in three touchdowns. Brown, who also had a passing strike for six, was efficient. He picked Nebraska’s secondary apart at will, continually finding open receivers in critical situations. The Hawkeyes ran for 156 yards as a team, led by 76 from L.J. Phillips, Jr. Related: Texas Tech Shows Incredible Grit, Toughness To Be College Football Playoff Contender And it wasn’t like Nebraska’s offense was struggling. They moved the ball, putting up 153 yards in the air and 107 on the ground. The explosive play was never really there. And Anthony Colandrea had an interception and was limited to minus-12 rushing yards. Huskers Have One More Chance To Gain Momentum This might be one of the biggest bowl games in Nebraska’s history in quite some time. The Huskers need momentum back on their side heading into the offseason. They are likely to be sent to a mid-level bowl game, such as the Cactus Bowl, Music City Bowl or Duke’s Mayo Bowl. After the loss to Iowa, the chances of a bigger draw were erased. Regardless, Nebraska coming out, performing well and earning just the second postseason win since 2014 would be critical for Rhule and his staff. Read more at Sportsnaut

item.title: George Russell drops cryptic hint over where Toto Wolff “stands off the record” on Max Verstappen
item.description: Motorsport photo Toto Wolff has spent the past week sounding remarkably unfazed by Formula 1’s fiercest driver feud. George Russell , however, just hinted that Mercedes ’ team principal sounds rather different once the microphones are switched off. Speaking exclusively to Martin Brundle for Sky Sports F1 - in an interview previewed Friday ahead of its full broadcast before Sunday’s Qatar Grand Prix - Russell was pressed on Wolff’s diplomatic public stance toward Max Verstappen following their Las Vegas flashpoint. Russell stopped short of repeating private conversations, but left little doubt that Wolff’s off-camera assessment carries a sharper edge. "Well, I know where he [Wolff] stands off the record, so I won't probably repeat that," Russell said. "Toto and I were flying back after the race in Vegas, and we did have quite a laugh about the comments that were said after the race. But we just know how certain people go about their business." Why Wolff’s Las Vegas tone raised eyebrows That remark cuts straight into one of the paddock’s most scrutinised dynamics. Wolff’s public warmth toward Verstappen has been tracked closely ever since Mercedes pursued the Red Bull driver in 2025 - talks Russell himself confirmed to Sky Sports F1 in June 2025 had delayed his own contract renewal. Even after Wolff publicly shut down fresh rumours in March 2026 - insisting "The Max to Mercedes thing for now is not on" and backing Russell to stay with Brackley "until 2037" - photographs of Wolff and Verstappen holidaying together surfaced again in July 2026, keeping the speculation alive. Last weekend in Nevada put that dynamic back under the microscope. After final-practice contact at Turn 14 triggered public criticism from Russell, Verstappen answered by winning Saturday night’s Grand Prix while Russell clipped the barrier late while battling team-mate Kimi Antonelli and dropped to ninth. In the aftermath, Verstappen declared Russell "so far below my level" and took open satisfaction in his rival’s late error. Toto Wolff, Executive Director of Mercedes AMG Petronas F1 Team, George Russell, Mercedes AMG Petronas F1 Team Toto Wolff, Executive Director of Mercedes AMG Petronas F1 Team, George Russell, Mercedes AMG Petronas F1 Team Wolff’s public reaction, by contrast, stayed conspicuously calm. Calling Verstappen "a deserving winner" who "made no mistakes" and "always had a response," Wolff brushed off the tension between the pair. "It's probably been a bit of cat and mouse," Wolff told reporters, adding that "these provocations in either side is another good factor of entertainment" while noting only that there had been "a bit of an exchange" in the stewards’ room. Timing explains part of that restraint: Wolff’s initial paddock remarks came shortly after the chequered flag, before Verstappen’s sharpest press-conference digs had fully made the rounds. item.title: Vero Beach football reaches state semifinals for second straight year
item.description: VERO BEACH — For the second consecutive year, Vero Beach football is headed back to the Florida state semifinals. The Fighting Indians defeated Edgewater 38-23 on Friday, Nov. 27 at Billy Livings Field at the Citrus Bowl to advance to the FHSAA Class 6A state semifinals. Vero Beach (12-1) will be making its first back-to-back state semifinal appearances since 1993-94. The Fighting Indians will learn their semifinal opponent after the conclusion of the remaining region finals. DeLand (11-1), which is ranked below Vero Beach in the latest MaxPreps state rankings, has already advanced to the Class 6A state semifinals. Vero Beach jumped all over Edgewater in the first half, building a 24-3 lead behind a touchdown pass from Makai White to Marcus Melbourne Jr. and touchdown runs by Jayden Lockhart and Marc Johns. The Fighting Indians piled up 269 total yards, including 200 on the ground, while limiting Edgewater to just 59. Lockhart added another rushing score early in the third quarter, ballooning Vero Beach's advantage to 31-3. Edgewater (8-5) battled back with a pair of touchdowns to cut the deficit to two scores, but Lockhart iced the game midway through the fourth quarter with his third rushing touchdown. item.title: “Not Gonna Put Myself Out There”: Kim Mulkey Reveals Her Intentions Around Ongoing Legal Battle Between LSU and the SEC
item.description: November 2, 2026: LSU Head Coach Kim Mulkey is introduced prior to NCAA, College League, USA Women s Basketball game action between the Southeastern Louisiana Lions and the LSU Tigers at the Pete Maravich Assembly Center in Baton Rouge, LA. /CSM Baton Rouge USA – ZUMAc04_ 20261102_zma_c04_039 Copyright: xJonathanxMailhesx ©IMAGO/ZUMA Press Wire Kim Mulkey has never been one to shy away from speaking her mind, but LSU’s ongoing legal battle with the SEC has put the head coach in a position where she would rather keep her opinions to herself. With the conference threatening the Tigers’ membership amid an escalating dispute over eligibility rules, the stakes are extending far beyond any one athletic program. Mulkey, meanwhile, has made it clear she isn’t willing to join a battle where her voice may carry little weight. During the press conference following LSU’s 84-65 win over Villanova, Kim Mulkey replied to a question from beat reporter Mike Scarbrough when he asked about her opinion on the ongoing lawsuit. Her response was recorded and posted to X by Scarbrough himself. “I have lots of opinions about it, but I’m not gonna put myself out there because I’m an employee at LSU, and really, they don’t care what I think.” The dispute between LSU and the SEC stems from eligibility questions stemming from former professional athletes on the college’s rosters, with the conference arguing that the Tigers’ actions have threatened its ability to enforce rules agreed upon by member institutions. Kim Mulkey's stance on LSU's legal showdown with the SEC could reshape women's college basketball politics. Subscribe for insider analysis on how this dispute unfolds. It all began when former St. John’s star RJ Luis Jr. tried to join LSU’s men’s basketball roster despite having played in NBA preseason games and previously holding a professional contract with both the Utah Jazz and the Boston Celtics following his last year in college, the 2024-25 season. He was blocked by both the NCAA and the SEC from competing, with each citing rules stemming from its eligibility criteria. However, two preliminary injunctions delivered in Louisiana court prevented either of them from stopping Luis, giving LSU the legal authority to roster and play him. The first injunction was delivered on August 24, while the latter was released on November 13. Following the second injunction, the SEC let LSU know in writing that it would comply with the court’s ruling and would not fine or penalize the team in any way. item.description: DENVER, CO - NOVEMBER 22: Fernando Mendoza #15 of the Las Vegas Raiders throws a pass during the fourth quarter against the Denver Broncos at Empower Field at Mile High on November 22, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. The Broncos defeated the Raiders 38-24. (Photo by Justin Edmonds/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Cleveland Browns take on the Las Vegas Raiders this Sunday. The Browns are a perfect 4-0 at home and coming off of a bye week. The Raiders have lost both starts with new quarterback Fernando Mendoza , but that also doesn’t mean they’re a pushover. Here is what the national media is saying about the Week 12 game between the Browns and Raiders: NFL.com (Various) Why Gennaro picked the Raiders: Will the third start be the charm for Fernando Mendoza? In his debut as Las Vegas’ QB1, the No. 1 overall pick sprinted out of the gates with 10 points in the first two drives vs. Seattle … but he appeared to run out of steam when the Raiders ran out of scripted plays. While the Browns have been one of the league’s most pleasant surprises at 6-4, they’re not exactly beating teams into submission. In fact, according to NFL Research, Cleveland is the only team besides 1-9 Tennessee to have been tied or trailing in the fourth quarter of every game this season. item.title: Farrell senses 'shift' as Ireland finish 2026 strongly
item.description: Stuart McCloskey featured in all 12 Ireland Tests this year while Ulster team-mate James McNabney marked his second cap with two tries off the bench [Getty Images] Ireland's return to Twickenham may not have produced more viral moments like Stuart McCloskey barrelling Marcus Smith into touch, but it did yield the victory needed to close the book on what head coach Andy Farrell considers a successful year. Farrell has not shied away from his intention to use the November window as a World Cup test run: four weekends, four games, heavy-hitting opposition, six-day turnarounds. Friday's Nations Championship fifth-place play-off at a half-empty Allianz Stadium, however, felt like a comedown in the wake of a nail-biting win over world champions South Africa. But winning ugly is an important feature for the best teams and carving out a gritty 38-14 success over Australia is a reflection of the progress Farrell has been demanding to see. Casting his eye over the campaign as a whole, he sounded upbeat as he spoke about a noticeable uptick in his squad's desire to grow with the World Cup coming into view. "We've certainly seen a shift in our appetite to want to grow and get better," said Farrell. "That's been very evident in the camp. It transfers sometimes to games, sometimes it doesn't, but we've seen the step up as far as that's concerned. "It's been a very successful campaign for that alone, but we've got to keep that going now and taking big steps forward." Replicating the punchy, spirited display that brought down South Africa in Dublin last week was always going to be a big ask, and Ireland certainly showed signs of weariness during a clunky first-half display that a more accurate team than Australia would have punished. But by hook or by crook, Ireland went in at half-time with a 10-point lead before an improved second-half showing saw them dispatch Australia for the seventh time in a row. Tries by Robbie Henshaw, Nick Timoney, Rob Baloucoune, and a double from breakout back-rower James McNabney ultimately sealed Ireland's 10th win in 12 games in 2026. It was also enough to secure fifth place in the inaugural Nations Championship. Farrell, however, was more concerned about how his side adapted during a sticky Test match when neither side were at their best. "It was a stop-start game where things weren't really going our way," he added. "That was very similar [to the South Africa game] in the sense that we had no field position, no ball, a lot of that down to Australia, but most of it was down to ourselves as well, giving penalties away and not winning the ball we wanted to win. "But we still found a way to be clinical when we had an opportunity in their 22." item.title: Central Bucks West shuts out Spring-Ford, wins district championship
item.description: DOYLESTOWN — Central Bucks West played for its sixth PIAA District One football championship on Friday night. The Bucks won District One onfield titles under Mike Pettine in 1993 and 1997-99, as well as Mike Carey in 2000. Spring-Ford, like CB West, went into the game at War Memorial Field with identical 12-1 records. The Bucks finished the job, downing the Rams 34-0 behind a dominant rushing attack and suffocating defense. Senior Lou Cipollo ran for a pair of touchdowns while seniors Nick Miletto and Braylen Cope both scored a rushing touchdown. CB West will face the St. Joseph Prep/Nazareth winner in next weekend’s Class 6A semifinals. Prep led Nazareth 49-20 at the start of the fourth quarter. West had reached the district title game in 2022, when it lost at Garnet Valley, while Spring-Ford fell to Coatesville for the 2012 district championship. This is the Bucks' first district title in 26 seasons. Rob Rowan’s CB West squad defeated Perkiomen Valley 56-42, Central Bucks East 44-21 and Council Rock South 30-13 to reach the final, while Spring-Ford topped Quakertown 42-28, Plymouth Whitemarsh 28-21 and top-seeded Downingtown East 17-14 at districts. *Check back later tonight for much more on the game. What’s next for Spring-Ford Football? The season ended for the Rams. What’s next for Central Bucks West Football? The Bucks will face St. Joseph Prep or Nazareth in the state semifinals next weekend. item.title: Mangiapane Scores Twice, Blackhawks Beat Rangers For Fourth Straight Win
item.description: The Chicago Blackhawks (10-14-2) tied a franchise record for the fewest shots recorded in a regular-season game with 10, but it was enough to defeat the New York Rangers (13-11-1) 2-1 at the United Center on Friday. Andrew Mangiapane scored both of Chicago’s goals, his first two tallies of the season, Oliver Moore had two assists, and Spencer Knight stopped 30 of 31 shots as the Blackhawks extended their winning streak to four games. The Blackhawks are now 6-1-1 in eight games since an abysmal 0-3 Southeastern road trip earlier this month. Mika Zibanejad scored for the Rangers, while Dylan Garand started in net and allowed two goals on 10 shots faced. Adam Fox extended his point streak to five games with an assist on Zibanejad’s power-play goal. All three goals in Friday’s game were power-play tallies, with the Blackhawks converting on both opportunities and extending their goal streak to eight games. Since opening the season with a 5-for-51 stretch, the power play has now scored on 13 of its last 22 opportunities. Even without Patrick Kane and Tyler Bertuzzi , the man advantage continued its red-hot stretch, and it was the second unit stepping up to score both goals against the Rangers. Entering Friday, New York had the NHL’s top-ranked penalty kill and had allowed a league-low three power-play goals in their first 12 road games. But even without their best offensive players, including captain Connor Bedard and Bowen Byram , the power play impressively still found a way to generate all the offense needed against a stout Rangers’ PK for a fourth straight win. Defensively, Knight was outstanding for the second straight game, as the 25-year-old was credited with 2.03 goals saved above expected against the Rangers. Over his last three outings — all wins — Knight has stopped 92 of 97 shots for a .948 save percentage. While the Rangers outshot and outchanced the Blackhawks by a wide margin, they were credited with only 10 high-danger scoring chances at even strength. Much like Wednesday’s win in Seattle, the Hawks’ defense didn’t allow many threatening looks. The defensemen and forwards also selflessly stepped in the shooting lane, recording 22 blocked shots in Friday’s win. Here are highlights from the Blackhawks 2-1 win over the Rangers, moving their 2026-27 regular-season record to 10-14-2 in 26 games. First Period With Matt Rempe in the penalty box for boarding Kevin Korchinski , the scorching-hot Blackhawks power play hit the ice for the first time and converted. Moore poked a loose puck over to Mangiapane at the right circle, and he fired a one-timer past Garand for his first goal of the season at 4:23. 1-0, Chicago. item.title: The Galaxy keep missing the playoffs. Fans want ownership to take action
item.description: Galaxy forward Kyogo Furuhashi reacts during a match against Seattle at Dignity Health Sports Park on Sept. 12. After winning the MLS Cup title in 2024, the Galaxy haven't returned to the playoffs. (Luiza Moraes / Getty Images) Statistically, it’s far easier to make the MLS playoffs than it is to miss them. Eighteen of 30 teams qualify for the postseason, meaning each one starts the season with a 60% chance of making the playoffs. No other major professional sports league in the U.S. is as generous. Yet the Galaxy failed to make the cut this year. And last year. In fact, the Galaxy have missed the playoffs four times in six years since Greg Vanney took over as manager. They also missed in three of the four seasons before Vanney arrived, meaning the Galaxy have cleared the lowest playoff bar in American sports just three times in the last decade. And they haven’t done it in consecutive seasons since Bruce Arena was the coach. Read more: Mauricio Pochettino's exit places U.S. men's soccer in a precarious state Arena left a decade ago. (To be fair, the last time the Galaxy did reach the playoffs, in 2024, Vanney guided them to a championship .) But wait, there’s more. Home attendance was down, dropping below the 20,000 per-game average for the first time in a non-COVID season since the Galaxy left the Rose Bowl for Carson in 2003. That’s a decrease of more than 18% since 2023. All this should be concerning for the team and its owners at AEG. The Galaxy, after all, used to be the model MLS franchise. It won the most games, had the best players, collected the most titles and led the league in attendance nine times. Today? Not so much. So does AEG have a plan to fix that? We reached out to Dan Beckerman , AEG’s president and chief executive, through a company spokesman, hoping for some clues. We never heard back. However, general manager Will Kuntz , speaking in a videoconference with the media Friday, agreed things are dismal. “I don’t think we did a good enough job collectively last year,” he said. “So for us, it’s really about taking a hard look at everything we’ve done process-wise and saying ‘hey, how can we be better?’ Because it cannot continue like this.” Galaxy coach Greg Vanney reacts during a match against LAFC at BMO Stadium on Oct. 25. (Luke Hales / Getty Images) Yet Kuntz, the architect of the MLS Cup team, may not be around to see that process through. Vanney still has two years left on his lucrative contract while Kuntz’s deal ends next month, so if there’s going to be a fall guy for the Galaxy’s recent failures, it’s likely to be the GM, not the coach. On Friday, Kuntz was already speaking of the team in the past tense. “I really enjoyed my time at the Galaxy. I love being here,” he said. “I’d like to be back if it was up to me. But it’s not.” Nor is it up to the team’s most loyal supporters, who would like to see someone sacrificed for the team’s fall from grace. item.title: Cavan Sullivan named MLS Young Player of the Year 🌟
item.description: Cavan Sullivan named MLS Young Player of the Year 🌟 Philadelphia Union and USMNT midfielder Cavan Sullivan has capped a record-setting regular season by being named the 2026 MLS Young Player of the Year. In his first full campaign, the Man City-bound starlet emerged as one of the league's most exciting young talents, finishing with with a career-high 23 goal contributions (nine goals, 14 assists) in 29 appearances, and recorded a goal contribution in 10 consecutive matches, the longest such run by a teenager in MLS history. Both his total of 23 goal contributions and his 14 assists are the most ever by a teenager in a single MLS season. Sullivan's form also earned him MLS Player of the Month honors for September 2026. At 17 years and two days old, he became the youngest winner of the award in league history. His production on the club level soon translated to the international stage. Sullivan received his first call-up to the US men's national team in September and made his debut against Peru, becoming the second-youngest player in USMNT history to start a match. He has since collected four senior caps and added another milestone to his résumé by scoring against Mexico at 17 years and five days old, making him the youngest goalscorer in USMNT history.

item.title: How Columbus Crew turned it all around to set up MLS playoff showdown vs. Messi
item.description: It wasn’t working. Issa Tall had to admit that. Well, he didn’t really have to. The results told the story for him. The Columbus Crew didn’t win in its first five MLS matches. By the World Cup break, 15 games in, they’d only added two more. There needed to be changes, and they needed to be big. The Crew general manager moved quickly. In May, he fired coach Henrik Rydström, his first coaching hire as the Crew’s chief soccer officer, though he was quick to point out he was involved with previous hires including bringing in Wilfried Nancy. He spent big in the summer, revamping the Crew’s attack and adding pieces while bidding farewell to some regulars. Ten players arrived, and eight went out. It worked. The Crew turned the boat around, going from worst in the Eastern Conference to closing the season on a six-game win streak and having won eight of their last nine. That was enough not only to jump out of Thursday’s wild card match but to set up a First Round playoff series with Inter Miami, the reigning champion led by Lionel Messi. They also pushed to the U.S. Open Cup final, falling to St. Louis City in a penalty shootout. All of it led Tall to believe he made the right decisions, moving on quickly from the coach he thought was the right man for the job. “Some people could’ve waited the full year. Maybe it would’ve been safer, but that’s not me. That’s not us as a club. That’s not even the way we play!” Tall told USA TODAY Sports ahead of the playoffs. “You see how we are bold and are not afraid of taking risk. At the end of the day, it wasn’t even a risk necessarily. It was necessary for our players, for our club as a whole and I think ultimately we made the right decision to do it at that time.” Tall still stands by Rydström as a good coach, something he’s proving while leading Hammarby in Sweden which currently sits atop of the table after running off five consecutive wins. But he wasn’t the right fit for the Crew in the post-Nancy era. The Crew turned to Courtois, a former Crew academy and MLS Next Pro coach who continued the idea first expressed on the field so successfully by Nancy’s teams. The squad might not have been the entirely right squad, either. Tall turned to a scouting network led by Mark Nichols, bringing in a proven MLS veteran in Santi Rodriguez, Chile national team forward Gonzalo Tapia, securing a loan deal for Moroccan winger Anass Zaroury and signing designated player Brais Mendez, a Spanish attacker whose arrival from Real Sociedad brought to mind that of Cucho Hernandez. While Mendez is at a different stage of his carer than Hernandez was, he turned into a star in Columbus, showing his full potential in MLS after frustrating stints with Watford and loans in Huseca, Mallorca and Getafe. item.title: Gotham FC’s title defense comes to crushing end in semifinal loss after venue change
item.description: They came by car, by the special-event X80 bus, by bike if they were feeling sporty. They came in layers, in beanies and scarves, with Gotham’s black-and-sky-blue colors on top. They came on behalf of those who couldn’t come, capacity being reduced at this impromptu change of venue, each one trying to make noise for five. Gotham FC forward Sam Kerr (20) competes for the ball against Kansas City Current defender Gabrielle Robinson (24) on Sunday, Nov. 15, 2026, in New York City. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect They came with some measure of outrage — these home-field shenanigans would never happen in men’s sports — while their better angels told them to come in joy, in celebration, everyone watching women’s sports. And then, 25 miles and 20,000 seats removed from their regular destination at New Jersey’s Sports Illustrated Stadium, huddled in the bleachers by a blue track ringing an immaculate pitch at Icahn Stadium on Randall’s Island, in the shadow of the old Psychiatric Center and with the light fading over the Costco across the river, 5,000 devoted souls Sunday afternoon watched Gotham’s NWSL title defense end in a 2-1 semifinal loss to the Kansas City Current. “We lost today because we weren’t the better team,” Gotham winger and oracle Midge Purce said. “That being said, I would say it’s inexcusable. It’s not what you want in a professional league. It’s not what you want for women who are progressing in the United States and supposed to be one of the best leagues in the entire world. I think it’s a bad look for everyone involved. And we always want to be at Sports Illustrated in front of our fans when we earned that right throughout the season. But I would say it had no effect on performance today.” The match had been moved to Icahn on Monday due to concerns over the disintegrating field conditions at Sports Illustrated, which had unfortunately overshadowed Gotham’s quarterfinal victory there last weekend. Gotham was unbeaten in its past 13 matches at Sports Illustrated, which is operated by the Red Bulls of MLS. Croix Bethune, left, celebrates scoring a goal with Kansas City Current teammate Lo’eau LaBonta during an NWSL playoff match in New York, Nov. 15, 2026. Getty Images “I think that’s also part of the sadness,” head coach Juan Carlos Amorós said. “I think we never know what would have happened if we played on a good pitch. I think it was the right decision to come here. I think the pitch in the other stadium was unfortunately unplayable.” Tickets for the semifinal were reallotted and grabbed up in a hurry, while Gotham officials ground on the logistics of moving their game-day operations. “Obviously not ideal we had to change stadiums, but … I think that’s really awesome to come into a new environment, a new stadium, you have to adapt, you have to make sure you can bring that energy and our supporters did that tonight and that’s incredible,” Gotham midfielder Savannah McCaskill said. item.title: Beckham to be inducted into US Soccer Hall of Fame
item.description: David Beckham was knighted by King Charles in 2025 [Getty Images] David Beckham will be inducted into the United States' National Soccer Hall of Fame as part of its 2027 class. The former Manchester United and England midfielder, 51, made headlines in 2007 when he moved to Los Angeles from Spanish giants Real Madrid to join Major League Soccer (MLS) side LA Galaxy on a five-year contract. He made 124 appearances in all competitions for Galaxy, scoring 20 goals, and twice won both the MLS Cup and Supporters' Shield. Beckham's six seasons at Galaxy helped to raise the global profile of MLS and following his retirement in 2013, he became co-owner of MLS club Inter Miami, who signed Argentina World Cup winner Lionel Messi in 2023. His induction ceremony is set to take place on 16 April 2027 in Frisco, Texas. David Beckham's deal with LA Galaxy in 2007 was reportedly worth £128m [Getty Images] He was told the news he had been chosen on the veterans' ballot at an MLS board of governors' meeting on Thursday and said his time in the US has been "an incredible journey". Beckham, who had two loan spells with AC Milan in 2009 and 2010 while at Galaxy, added: "I'm looking to build this league and this sport in this great country for a long time." Meanwhile, former US internationals Megan Rapinoe and Julie Ertz have also been voted into the Hall of Fame in their first year of eligibility. Ballon d'Or winner Rapinoe, 41, and midfielder Ertz, 34, lifted the Women’s World Cup twice with with the US in 2015 and 2019. "To be alongside all the greatest players that have played for us, and played for our country alongside a bunch of my team-mates and friends, recognised like that in this way just means you were successful and a part of great teams," Rapinoe wrote on Instagram. item.title: Gotham FC’s home semifinal moved to 5K-seat stadium in field quality debacle
item.description: Seattle Reign FC defender Phoebe McClernon, left, defends Gotham FC forward Guro Reiten during an NWSL playoff game in Harrison, N.J., Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. For the first time in franchise history, Gotham FC is set to host its semifinal match next weekend. But there’s an unfortunate twist. Gotham’s semifinal match against the Kansas City Current won’t be played at the club’s typical stomping grounds in Harrison, New Jersey. Instead, Gotham agreed to move Sunday’s match to Icahn Stadium on Randall’s Island for better playing surface quality. “This was an extremely difficult decision, and one we did not take lightly,” Gotham president of soccer operations Yael Averbuch West said in a letter to fans. “After thoughtful consultation with coach Juan Carlos Amorós, our team captains, and our ownership, we felt it was important to prioritize a playing surface that appropriately allows our athletes to perform at their best. Providing our players with a high-quality surface to compete is a responsibility we take very seriously.” The Gotham FC starting eleven line up before the NWSL playoff quarterfinal in Harrison, N.J., Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. Lev Radin/Shutterstock Gotham is a tenant of Major League Soccer’s Red Bull New York at Sports Illustrated Stadium. The Red Bulls are scheduled to play an exhibition game there Saturday night, exacerbating concerns about the field quality. The state of Sports Illustrated Stadium’s pitch has been a cause for concern over the past two weeks. ESPN reported the NWSL fined Gotham $10,000 for poor field conditions during last week’s regular-season finale, after which the club was awarded its first league Shield. The pitch condition was once again a major sticking point after Gotham’s ugly quarterfinal win against the Seattle Reign. Retiring Reign midfielder Jess Fishlock called the field “atrocious.” Gotham defender Jess Carter was overheard saying the grounds were “so bad” when walking through the tunnel after the match. A week after Jaelin Howell injured her right ankle during a home game, the Gotham midfielder said the field was “pretty sandy” and “a little unstable.” Amorós acknowledged the rough conditions impacted the quality of the game. Seattle Reign FC defender Phoebe McClernon, left, defends Gotham FC forward Guro Reiten during an NWSL playoff game in Harrison, N.J., Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. Corey Sipkin for the NY POST “At this level, in this kind of game, as a league, and we should have a better surface,” Amorós said. “Unfortunately, our club and football club did absolutely everything in their power to make sure that was the case. Unfortunately, it wasn’t. But luckily, it looks like nobody got hurt, and the game was what it was.” It’s not immediately clear if the NWSL penalized Gotham for a second consecutive week because of the field. item.title: NYCFC fires head coach Pascal Jansen after second-half collapse
item.description: NYCFC has fired head coach Pascal Jansen. New York City FC will be looking for a new head coach this offseason. Less than 24 hours after the club played its final match of the 2026 season, NYCFC announced that it fired head coach Pascal Jansen following a disappointing campaign that saw the club miss the playoffs for only the third time in its 12-year history. NYCFC went through an ugly 2026 season, finishing 11th in the Eastern Conference and being knocked out of playoff contention before the club even reached its Decision Day matchup with D.C. United on Saturday. The rough season was highlighted by the massive second-half collapse NYCFC went through following the World Cup break, posting a 5W-8D-6L record and sliding from eighth place to 11th. Jansen was informed of the decision by the club’s front office on Sunday morning and ultimately the decision to move on from him as head coach came down to the “failure of making playoffs” following a “disappointing season,” a source told The Post. NYCFC has fired head coach Pascal Jansen. Getty Images The head coaching role will take on an even bigger role going into 2027 as NYCFC prepares for massive changes with the planned move into their new stadium and MLS changing their league calendar to a summer-through-spring format, which is in line with the European football calendar and includes an abbreviated sprint season that will run from February to May. The club views this next year as a “crucial point in franchise history” and the feeling is that NYCFC wants to make sure it has “the right leadership in place,” the source added. NYCFC will begin its search for a new head coach immediately, sporting director Todd Dunivant said in a statement released late Sunday morning. “We would like to thank Pascal for his commitment and contributions to New York City FC and wish him and his family all the best. This decision follows a thorough review of the season and reflects our ambition as an organization,” he said. One of the biggest problems that NYCFC faced this season – especially during its struggles in the second half – had been allowing late goals that would cost the club points, or matches altogether. And the club dealt with a number of injuries during the course of the season, while also playing much of the year without one of its top scorers, Alonso Martinez, as he recovered from a torn ACL he suffered last fall. item.title: Messi makes history with MLS Golden Boot
item.description: Messi retired from international football with Argentina earlier this year [Getty Images] Inter Miami forward Lionel Messi has become the first player in MLS history to win the Golden Boot in consecutive seasons. The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner scored 26 goals in 31 appearances, four clear of FC Dallas striker Peter Musa and five more than Nashville's English forward Sam Surridge. Messi becomes only the sixth player to land the award twice, joining a list that includes former Charlton Athletic and Southampton striker Bradley Wright-Phillips. In addition to his goals, the 39-year-old notched 17 assists over the course of the MLS season, ensuring his 43 goal contributions was also a league best for the second year in a row. And the World Cup winner could soon make more history as he bids to become the first three-time Landon Donovan MLS MVP winner. The former Argentina forward landed the award in 2024 as Inter Miami won the Supporters' Shield title and also in 2025 as they won the MLS Cup. Despite Messi's magic, Miami weren't able to land top spot in the MLS Eastern Conference, with the team finishing 17 points behind Surridge's Nashville. They will now face Columbus Crew over three games in the first round of the MLS Cup play-offs which begin later this month.
